findings.title: Out-of-bounds write in mm_decode_pal via unchecked start+i palette index
findings.message: mm_decode_pal() reads a 16-bit 'start' offset and a 16-bit 'count' directly from the bitstream (both attacker-controlled, up to 65535) and then writes 'count' consecutive unsigned ints into s->palette[start+i] without ever validating that start+i stays within the bounds of the palette array (unsigned int palette[AVPALETTE_COUNT], i.e. 256 entries). Because bytestream2_get_le16() imposes no limit on the returned value, an attacker-crafted MM video stream can supply start and/or count values large enough to make start+i exceed 255, causing writes far past the end of the MmContext::palette array. This is a heap/struct out-of-bounds write (the OSS-Fuzz report calls it out-of-array access), which can corrupt adjacent heap memory and potentially lead to memory corruption or code execution.
findings.suggestion: Mask or clamp the palette write index to the valid range of the palette array (0..AVPALETTE_COUNT-1), e.g. by ANDing (start+i) with 0xFF as done in the actual fix, or by validating that start and count keep start+i within bounds before performing the write, and rejecting/truncating the loop otherwise.

ground_truth.root_cause: The refactor in commit 63ea1660fa ("avcodec/mm: decode partial palette") replaced a previous fixed 128-iteration loop with a stream-controlled 'start' offset and 'count' loop bound, but failed to mask/clamp the resulting array index (start+i) to the valid range of the palette array, allowing attacker-controlled values to index arbitrarily far outside the array.
